title: The semipermutation map is a bijection exchanging the descent number with the lecture hall statistic
author: Giovanni Gaiffi and Giovanni Interdonato
work: Generalizing Eulerian Numbers via Semipermutations: Topological and Combinatorial Aspects
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 5.11 of the article (source label thm:bijection, source0.tex lines 838--844), the main bijection of the paper: the recursively defined map $\psi$ on the set $W$ of semipermutations is a well defined bijection sending the descent number to the lecture hall statistic, $\des(w)=\lec(\psi(w))$, and it restricts to a bijection of each symmetric group $\mathcal S_n$. It is delivered with the authors' own complete 47-line proof at source0.tex lines 846--892. H2: the proof is an original inductive construction on words rather than a qualifying examination exercise. The solver must run the induction on the length of $w$, verify that $\psi(w)$ is a rearrangement of $w$ by combining the inductive hypothesis on $w\setminus\sw(w)$ with the rearrangement $\delta$ of the special subword, prove injectivity by recovering $w$ from $\psi(w)$, and then track how the descent number of $w$ transforms into the lecture hall statistic of $\psi(w)$, including the restriction to permutations. Reproducing that recursive bijection with its statistic exchange is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
